title: vme-stack site file
description: One file per site. Shape and formats only; rules that span fields (unique IP/MAC, IP inside the subnet, driver exists) are checked in preflight.

site.description: Short site name, used for run logs and Terraform state keys.

hvm_iso.description: Path of the stock HVM install ISO on the deploy server.

seed_mode.description: How the seed reaches the installer. Only 'embedded' (seed inside a per-host ISO) is implemented.

vme_iso.description: Path of HPE's VM Essentials software ISO (contains the Manager qcow2.gz) on the deploy server. Required with vme_manager.

network.description: The management network all hosts share.

mgmt_vlan.description: 802.1Q tag of the mgmt network, 0 = untagged. With nic layout 'shared' it must be the switch port's native VLAN.

ntp.description: NTP servers (IPv4 addresses or host names) for systemd-timesyncd.

proxy.description: HTTP proxy the installer and apt use, e.g. http://proxy.example.com:3128.

bond_mode.description: Linux bond mode for bond0/bond1 (the official HPE guide uses active-backup).

compute_vlans.description: VLAN tags for VM traffic on the compute bridge, for cluster creation. Not passed to hpe-vm --install (its -v puts the Manager itself on that VLAN).

deploy_server.description: The machine that builds the per-host ISOs and serves them over HTTP to BMCs/hypervisors. It sits on (or routes to) the mgmt network; SSH, DNS and NTP are probed from it. Usually also where the EE runs.

address.description: Address hosts and BMCs fetch media from (default host of the media URL); with connection ssh also the address Ansible connects to.

user.description: Login on the deploy server for connection ssh, with passwordless sudo (an existing account, e.g. created by whoever set up the server). With connection local the playbook's own user is used and needs passwordless sudo.

ssh_private_key.description: Private key file on the controller (where the playbook or the EE runs) for user on the deploy server; also used for jump. Relative paths are relative to the site file. Never commit it.

jump.description: Optional SSH jump host (user@host) the controller goes through to reach the deploy server and the HVM hosts, logging in with deploy_server.ssh_private_key. Omit when the controller reaches them directly.

www_root.description: Directory nginx serves; ISOs go to <www_root>/isos/.

media_url.description: Base URL BMCs/hypervisors use to fetch media, if not http://<address>:<port>.

connection.description: How Ansible reaches the deploy server: ssh (default; address + user + ssh_private_key) or local (Ansible runs directly on the deploy server, without a container). From the EE container always use ssh, also when the container runs on the deploy server itself: 'local' would act inside the container (packages, nginx, ISO mount would land there).

access.description: access is replaced: access.ssh_private_key -> deploy_server.ssh_private_key (the deploy server's login) and defaults.hvm_ssh_private_key (the HVM hosts' login; both may name the same file); access.jump -> deploy_server.jump.

defaults.description: Per-host settings; any host can override them (except nic_layout, which hosts set as nics.layout).

vme_manager.description: The VME Manager VM, deployed with HPE's `hpe-vm --install` onto one HVM host. Netmask, gateway and DNS come from network.

host.description: Name of the HVM host (from hosts) that runs the Manager VM.

url.description: Appliance URL users and agents reach the Manager on. Default https://<ip>. With a name, every network.dns server must resolve it to ip (preflight checks).

size.description: hpe-vm size: S = 12 GB / 2 vCPU, M = 16 GB / 4 vCPU, L = 32 GB / 4 vCPU.

admin_user.description: Admin user hpe-vm sets up on the Manager VM, also the Manager's first admin (first-time setup).

admin_password.description: Password of admin_user on the Manager VM and in the Manager (best a vault reference).

tenant.description: Master tenant name set at first-time setup. Default: site.

email.description: Email of the Manager's first admin user (required by setup). Default: <admin_user>@<network.domain>.

license_key.description: VME license key (best a vault reference). Omit for the trial.

datastore.description: Cluster datastore (a datastores name of the cluster that holds vme_manager.host) to move the Manager VM's disk to once the cluster exists, e.g. shared NFS instead of the host's local disk. Done through the Manager's own server reconfigure; the local copy is kept.

autostart.description: libvirt autostart for the Manager VM on its host (hpe-vm leaves it off). Default false: off is enforced; true turns it on. Do not combine with HA failover of the Manager (a recovering host would start a second copy).

ssh_private_key.description: Private key the Manager uses to SSH into the hosts of every cluster (a key just for the Manager; best a vault reference). Required with vme_clusters.

ssh_public_key.description: The matching public key, added to the cluster hosts' admin user: the key line itself or a vault reference.

vme_groups.description: Manager groups (found by name or created). Clouds are added to them (vme_clouds.groups).

vme_clouds.description: Manager clouds (found by name or created): 'hvm' = HPE VM private cloud that holds HVM clusters, 'vmware' = VMware vCenter integration. Needs vme_manager.

type.description: hvm: private cloud for HVM clusters; vmware: vCenter cloud (needs vcenter).

groups.description: vme_groups names the cloud belongs to (at least one). The cloud is added to each; other clouds of a group stay.

url.description: vCenter address, e.g. https://vcenter.example.com (the Manager's API URL https://vcenter.example.com/sdk; /sdk is added when missing).

username.description: vCenter user (a read-only role is enough for the Manager's sync): a plain value or a vault reference.

cluster.description: Limit the cloud to this vCenter cluster. Default: the whole datacenter.

import_existing.description: Import the vCenter's existing VMs into the Manager (instances in the Manager's records; nothing changes in vCenter), switched on once the cloud's first sync is done. false skips the import.

credentials.description: vcenter.credentials is replaced by vcenter.username and vcenter.password, e.g. username: "{{ vault_vcenter.username }}", password: "{{ vault_vcenter.password }}".

vme_clusters.description: HVM clusters the Manager creates from the hosts (Manager API). Needs vme_manager with ssh_private_key/ssh_public_key.

cloud.description: vme_clouds name (type hvm) the cluster belongs to.

group.description: vme_groups name the cluster is placed in; one of its cloud's groups. Default: the cloud's first group.

hosts.description: Names of the hosts in the cluster (each host in at most one cluster). All must use the same mgmt/compute interface names and admin user.

layout.description: Cluster layout code, e.g. mvm-1.3-ubuntu-24.04-std-morpheus-amd64. Default: the newest standard HVM layout the Manager offers (mvm-<version>-ubuntu-24.04-std-morpheus-amd64; 1.2 on VME 8.1, 1.3 on 9.0).

datastores.description: Shared datastores added to the cluster (NFS for now; GFS2 later).

version.description: NFS version (Manager options: 3, 4). Omit for the default.

default.description: Image target: the default store for VM disks and images.

vme_cluster.description: Replaced by vme_groups, vme_clouds and vme_clusters (and vme_manager.ssh_private_key/ssh_public_key); see ansible/examples.

name.description: Lowercase host label: letters, digits, hyphens, not all digits, max 63 chars.

platform.description: How a host is booted from its ISO. manual: the pipeline publishes the ISO URL and waits; Terraform or a person attaches it and boots (VMs, servers without a BMC). redfish: HPE iLO or Dell iDRAC virtual media over Redfish (vendor detected at run time; role boot_redfish).

hvm_admin_user.description: Admin user on the HVM hosts, created by the install (key login + passwordless sudo). Not the Manager's admin (vme_manager.admin_user).

hvm_ssh_private_key.description: Private key file on the controller for hvm_admin_user on the HVM hosts. Its public key is installed for that user automatically (derived at preflight). Relative paths are relative to the site file; may be the same file as deploy_server.ssh_private_key. Never commit it.

items.description: OpenSSH public key line (ssh-ed25519, ssh-rsa or ecdsa).

hvm_ssh_keys.description: Extra public keys for hvm_admin_user (e.g. administrators' own keys), next to the one derived from hvm_ssh_private_key.

boot_disk.description: Disk the OS is installed on (LVM over the whole disk). 'auto' = the smallest disk (the installer skips its own media), a kernel device name such as /dev/sda, or installer match keys: all given keys must match. serial/model/vendor are glob patterns on the udev values ID_SERIAL/ID_MODEL/ID_VENDOR. ID_SERIAL is the /dev/disk/by-id/ name without its bus prefix (nvme-, ata-, scsi-): model + serial for NVMe/SATA, but often the WWN for SAS disks and RAID logical drives, so take it from by-id, not from the drive label. For a boot device, model is usually the simplest. No /dev/disk/by-* paths: the installer's path match only sees kernel names such as /dev/sda, which can change between boots on servers with several controllers; model/serial/id_path are stable.

oneOf.description: Kernel device name, e.g. /dev/sda or /dev/nvme0n1 (same as {path: ...}). Simple, but such names can change between boots on servers with several controllers.

path.description: Glob on the kernel device name, e.g. '/dev/sda' (not /dev/disk/by-*: the installer does not see those).

size.description: Among the matching disks, take the smallest or largest.

nic_layout.description: dedicated: bond0 = mgmt, bond1 = compute. shared: bond0 carries both, IP untagged.

hvm_admin_password.description: Password of hvm_admin_user (best a vault reference). Set in post-install; password SSH login is allowed for that user only. Needed by vme_clusters (the Manager logs in with it); all hosts of a cluster must use the same value.

admin_user.description: admin_user is renamed hvm_admin_user (the hosts' admin user; the Manager's is vme_manager.admin_user).

admin_password.description: admin_password is renamed hvm_admin_password, and takes a vault reference: hvm_admin_password: "{{ vault_hvm_admin_password }}".

ssh_keys.description: ssh_keys is replaced by hvm_ssh_private_key (the controller's key for the hosts; its public key is installed automatically) and hvm_ssh_keys (extra public keys only).

nics.description: NIC MACs per role, matched by MAC in netplan. 'layout' overrides defaults.nic_layout.

netplan.description: Raw netplan for edge cases, written verbatim into the seed (autoinstall network:). Instead of nics. Validated in preflight with netplan's own parser on the deploy server. The host's ip must be a static address on hpe_vm.mgmt_interface.

hpe_vm.description: Interfaces HPE's cluster join uses (build-ovs.sh -m/-c); required with netplan, derived from the layout with nics.

mgmt_interface.description: Interface carrying the host's ip (ethernet, bond or VLAN), static.

compute_interface.description: Interface for VM traffic; must not be the parent of the mgmt VLAN.

bmc.description: BMC (iLO/iDRAC) for platform redfish, with its own login: username and password (best vault references).

bios_setup.description: Let the pipeline set BIOS BootMode=Uefi and Secure Boot off before the install. Off by default: the customer's BIOS is not touched unless asked.

credentials.description: bmc.credentials is replaced by bmc.username and bmc.password, e.g. username: "{{ vault_ilo.username }}", password: "{{ vault_ilo.password }}".

storage.description: Raw autoinstall storage section for edge cases (RAID, partitioning, ...), written verbatim into the seed. Instead of boot_disk.

host.description: A host gets its network either from a nics layout (common cases, generated) or from raw netplan + hpe_vm (edge cases, used verbatim); disk from boot_disk (common) or raw storage (edge cases).

secret.description: A password or key. Plain text works, but a vault reference is recommended, e.g. "{{ vault_hvm_admin }}" or "{{ vault_ilo.password }}" (quoted): Ansible resolves it from the vault (group_vars/all/vault.yml next to the site file) when it is used. Any Ansible template is accepted.
